name: Badminton House
note: 1709 Britannia Illustrata plate ('one of the Seats of the Most Noble & Potent Prince Henry Duke of Beaufort'); the house and its formal park survive (National Trust); the second impression (RP-P-1949-370) is the documented duplicate drop; the point is the house's P625

name: Temple Newsam
note: Britannia Illustrata plate 42, 1707-09 ('the Seat of the Rt. Hon. ble Arthur Lord Ingram Viscount Irwin'); the house survives (National Trust). The Commons description is the Hepworth boilerplate followed by the plate's own title ('Showing Temple Newsam. The engraving is entitled: ...') - the 566 px 'Temple Newsam Kip.jpg' impression has an empty desc, this 3576 px file does not - and it agrees with the title verified from the British Museum M,21.42 and five other sources in all identifying particulars (checked 2026-10-13). The file's MediaInfo item carries no P180 from this VM (checked 2026-10-13, also on a file with a rich item), so the staged row ties by caption (the stored desc names the house); the point is the house's P625

name: Hutton Hall
note: 1709 Britannia Illustrata plate ('Hutton-in-the-Forest Hall, seat of Sir George Fletcher'); the Cumbrian Fletcher-Vane seat (pele tower, 1680 hall, 1730s walled garden, all Grade I) - NOT the Derbyshire parish of the same name; the point is the house's P625

name: Stanway House
note: 1709 Britannia Illustrata plate ('the seat of John Tracey Esq'); the Jacobean manor and its baroque water gardens survive ('Charteris' in the Rijksmuseum note is the Wemyss surname of the present owners, the TRACYS of Stanway); the point is the house's P625

name: Stoke House
note: 1709 Britannia Illustrata plate ('the seat of Sr. Thomas Cann' - son of Sir Robert Cann, Bristol MP and Mayor, who built the manor 1669); the house (Grade II*) still stands, now Trinity Theological College, Bristol. No Wikidata item for the house (the suburb is Q7618438; the enwiki article is 'Stoke Bishop'); the point is the Nominatim/OSM amenity point 51.4767404, -2.6294812 (checked 2026-10-13, 0 m)

name: Burford House
note: 1707 plate (Yale B2017.35.1, 'the House at Windsor, Belonging to his Grace Charles Beauclerck' - the duke of St Albans' house, Nell Gwyn's former house on the edge of Home Park); the house is GONE (sold to George III 1779, absorbed into the Royal Mews) but the view is locked to the standing Windsor Castle (Q42646) in the same view. No enwiki article ('Burford House' is a 4-way disambiguation with a red Windsor link; the house is described in the 'Nell Gwyn' article, which this row's wikipedia carries). The point is the Mews/Saint Alban's Street site from two geograph photos' WGS-84 EXIF (51.481051,-0.605551 / 51.480870,-0.605556; Nominatim 'Royal Mews, Windsor' 72 m from it, same street), ~325 m SOUTH of the castle's P625, checked 2026-10-13

name: St James's Palace
note: two 1707 plates (Yale B2017.35.3 'Le Palais Royal de St James' and B1977.14.18146 'The Palace and Park of St James's') - one site, one row per plate; the palace and its park stand; the point is the palace's P625

name: Lambeth Palace
note: 1711-12 plate (Yale B1977.14.17372, 'His Grace the Lord Archbishop of Canterbury Palace'); the palace stands (the archbishop of Canterbury's London residence); the point is the palace's P625

name: Somerset House
note: 1707 Britannia Illustrata plate (Yale B1977.14.18272; the Yale record's '1711-31' is the plate's later state - BM bmimages 00067960001 'Britannia Illustrata, print, London. 1707, this state later' and DCMS GAC 659 'published 1707' are the two independent sources); the QID is the 1964 LSE rebuilding on the original's site (part of the original Strand-side complex survives); Q110073896 is the item for the KIP ENGRAVING (not usable) and Q17542634 is a different Somerset House (Whitehaven) - the name-search trap check shows what the live caption route would resolve; the point is the site's P625

name: Hampton Court Palace
note: 1707 plate (the AIC's clean single-plate impression); the palace and its parterres stand. The Hampton Court trap in reverse: THIS is the palace on the Thames - a new site, distinct from the hand-tied Q1443802 'Hampton Court' in Herefordshire; the point is the palace's P625

name: Kings Weston House
note: 1710 plate ('Birds-eye view of the Kingsweston estate', Atkyns' Glocestershire); the view shows the earlier Elizabethan house - the house standing on the site is the Vanbrugh rebuild of 1712-19 for the Southwells. No Wikidata item for the house (not the Bristol suburb Q6413746, not the hill Q6413747); the point is the enwiki infobox WGS84 51.494382, -2.661541, which Nominatim/OSM 'Kings Weston House, Bristol' (51.4944124, -2.6614991) confirms to 4 m (checked 2026-10-13). The article's own grid ref ST529771 converts to 1.3 km W of that (the article's two position statements disagree) - it is NOT an independent confirmation, the infobox/OSM pair is (docs/lead_kip.md §2)
